headline: Supervised models on omics data gain generalizability via representation and bias control
label: Supervised Prediction From Molecular Data
summary: Recent preprints and published studies pair foundation-model embeddings, feature screening, and bias correction with molecular classifiers.
synthesis: Across these items, the dominant thread is supervised prediction of a biological or clinical label from high-dimensional molecular data, with explicit attention to how inputs are represented and reduced. Pretrained or knowledge-derived representations appear in several works: RNA foundation model embeddings improve cross-cohort F1 to 0.83 from 0.68 across 12 endometriosis cohorts, and MARBLE aligns histopathology representations with LLM and protein language model embeddings of genomic biomarkers. Feature selection forms a second strand, including a benchmark finding BcorSIS most effective and fastest for omics classification and a weight-sharing Bayesian neural network for consistent selection in cancer expression data. Several items pair representation learning with explicit interpretability or bias correction, as in SHAP-guided CpG selection for epigenetic age and DeBias, which removes demographic-associated subspaces using control samples. Not all items share each element.
